newsitem.title: FRANCE: American Eagle orders $2.4 billion of small jets.
newsitem.headline: American Eagle orders $2.4 billion of small jets.

text.p: American Airlines' commuter carrier American Eagle announced orders Tuesday for up to 117 short-range passenger jets worth $2.4 billion, splitting the business between two rival manufacturers.
At the Paris air show, American Eagle said it ordered 25 70-seat regional jets from Bombardier of Canada worth $700 million and 42 50-seat aircraft from Embraer of Brazil, also worth $700 million.

American Eagle's senior vice president Peter Pappas said the carrier also took options on another 25 of Bombardier's Canadair CRJ 700 aircraft and 25 of Embraer's EMB-145 jets. The total value of the order with options was $2.4 billion.

American Eagle's move to buy regional jets comes after an overhaul of its operations and the recent settlement of a dispute with pilots at its larger sister carrier American Airlines over Eagle's plans to start operating the new planes.
Eagle currently flies 200 turboprop aircraft on routes covering 127 cities across the United States, Canada and the Caribbean and connecting into American Airlines' main hubs.
"We have spent the last two years restructuring Eagle to make it a leaner and more competitive regional carrier," Pappas said. "Now Eagle is ready to enter the jet arena."
Pappas said the new planes would add capacity and allow the airline to replace some of its turboprop aircraft.

"American Eagle is entering a new phase," he told reporters. "At the present time these aircraft will be growth aircraft, but over time we will be replacing some of our turboprops, depending on demand in the marketplace," he said.
"Eagle is running at big load factors ... and customers are demanding regional jets." Load factor measures how full a carrier's flights are.
The order makes American the launch customer for the Canadair CRJ 700, which will be powered by engines from General Electric Co. Deliveries are to start in the year 2001.
Bombardier was also trying to sell its 50-seat jetliner to American Eagle but officials said it was undercut on price.
"Quite simply the commercial terms on this aircraft were not acceptable to us," Bombardier Aerospace President Robert Brown told reporters.
"We are reorganizing ourselves and we feel we are going to be very competitive in the 50-seat category," he added. "We're not going to be in the same position ... in the future."
"The competition was fierce but at the end of the day Embraer emerged as our choice," Pappas said. "The EMB-145 is very efficient, capable and we expect, profitable."

The twin-engined Embraer aircraft will be powered by AE 3007A1 engines made by Allison Engine Co., the U.S. unit of Britain's Rolls-Royce Plc. Allison said the order was worth in excess of $275 million.
Stock of AMR Corp., parent of American Airlines and American Eagle, fell 37.5 cents to $95.25 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
